fatal_errors: The proposed homogenization-and-quenching intervention is unrelated to the target intervention of laser-assisted machining of DED-fabricated Ti33Nb28Cr11V11Ni17.

The claim that a 2100 °C homogenization treatment will refine grains is scientifically unjustified; high-temperature holding ordinarily promotes grain growth unless a separate refinement mechanism is demonstrated.
A fixed 2100 °C treatment may cause incipient or complete melting in some of the loosely specified candidate alloys, but no composition-specific solidus constraint is provided.
Neither cited source supports the proposed heat-treatment schedule, edge-dislocation-dominated mechanism, 1600 °C service condition, or predicted 10–20% strength increase.
explanation: The hypothesis only aligns at the broad level of refractory HEAs and elevated-temperature performance. It does not reconstruct the target material, DED initial state, laser preheating and machining parameters, approximately 800 °C softening boundary, conventional-machining baseline, or the measured reductions in cutting force, roughness, and work hardening. Its same-composition control and explicit falsification threshold are useful, but the alloy is not fixed, the optional anneal makes the intervention ambiguous, and the experiment does not control for grain growth or partial melting. The cited evidence discusses BCC phase prediction, irradiation, refractory-element selection, and solid-solution strengthening, not the central processing, microstructural, dislocation, or performance claims.
